sections.label: CNB drug operations and MDA amendments
sections.summary: CNB ran close to 1,500 drug operations in 2019, seizing drugs worth about S$6.3 million, and the MDA was amended in 2012 and 2019 to protect young persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2019, the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB), together with other Home Team agencies, conducted close to 1,500 drug operations across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The estimated market value of the drugs seized was about S$6.3 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: CNB has not yet detected any trend of drug syndicates deliberately targeting young persons, be it selling drugs to children and young persons, or recruiting them into the trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2012, the Misuse of Drugs Act (MDA) was amended to provide for an offence for any adult who causes or procures any young person to traffic or import drugs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The minimum punishment for such an offender is 10 years’ imprisonment and 10 strokes of the cane.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If the trafficker was found to be trafficking a Class A controlled drug to a young person, the minimum punishment would be 10 years' imprisonment and 10 strokes, double the normal rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2019, MDA was further amended to provide more protection to children below 16 years of age and young persons from the harms of drugs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It is now an offence for an adult who possesses illicit drugs, knowing that a child is likely to be present in a place, to knowingly or recklessly leave the drugs or drug utensils within easy access of the child.
